slides.title: The medical-surgical unit nurse is admitting a client who has cirrhosis with a h
text: Question: The medical-surgical unit nurse is admitting a client who has cirrhosis with a history of chronic hepatitis C. Reports poor appetite. Disoriented to time. Dull abdominal pain 5/10 numeric rating scale. Peripheral edema with 2+ depression of the feet. Client is receiving diuretic therapy.  Select 3 nursing interventions the nurse should include in the client’s care plan.
A. Initiate intake and output including stool consistency.
B. Assess the client’s neurological status every 4 hours.
C. Anticipate discontinuation of diuretic therapy.
D. Monitor the client for purpura and petechiae.
E. Ask the client about their sleep cycle.
F. Remind the client to limit intake of alcohol containing beverages.
Correct answers: A. Initiate intake and output including stool consistency.; D. Monitor the client for purpura and petechiae.; E. Ask the client about their sleep cycle.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Initiate intake and output including stool consistency.
• Monitor the client for purpura and petechiae.
• Ask the client about their sleep cycle.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Initiate intake and output including stool consistency.” – Tracks fluid balance and stool changes
• “Monitor the client for purpura and petechiae.” – Detects bleeding from impaired clotting
• “Ask the client about their sleep cycle.” – Sleep reversal suggests encephalopathy
Not correct:
• “Assess the client’s neurological status every 4 hours.” – Source recommends more frequent neuro checks
• “Anticipate discontinuation of diuretic therapy.” – Edema supports continued diuresis if tolerated
• “Remind the client to limit intake of alcohol containing beverages.” – Alcohol should be avoided, not merely limited
⚠ Your PowerPoints disagree with this quiz key.
• The quiz key is shown above (source-backed).
• Your PowerPoints also support: “Remind the client to limit intake of alcohol containing beverages.”
• Unit 7 - GI, slide 31: “Limit or decrease ETOH”

The quiz key leaves out “Remind the client to limit intake of alcohol containing beverages.” and its note says alcohol should be avoided entirely. Your GI slide says to limit or decrease ETOH, which supports that option. Because the question says to select 3, check with your instructor which three they want.

A. Respiratory rate and characteristics

text: Question: The registered nurse in the emergency department is caring for a 40-year-old client who has appendicitis and is experiencing localized right upper quadrant pain rated 9/10 on the numerical rating scale. The nurse is preparing to insert an 18-gauge IV.  Which of the following should the nurse include in the client’s care plan? Select all that apply.
A. Ensure catheter hub is covered with a moist skin barrier.
B. Review accuracy of IV solution order.
C. Assess the client’s body weight.
D. Monitor IV patency every 2 hours.
E. Evaluate IV insertion site every shift.
F. Remove catheter within 30 minutes if edema is observed around insertion site.
Correct answers: B. Review accuracy of IV solution order.; C. Assess the client’s body weight.; D. Monitor IV patency every 2 hours.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Review accuracy of IV solution order.
• Assess the client’s body weight.
• Monitor IV patency every 2 hours.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Review accuracy of IV solution order.” – Checks prescription accuracy
• “Assess the client’s body weight.” – Establishes baseline fluid status
• “Monitor IV patency every 2 hours.” – Checks ongoing IV function
Not correct:
• “Ensure catheter hub is covered with a moist skin barrier.” – Skin barrier should dry before securement
• “Evaluate IV insertion site every shift.” – Site needs more frequent assessment
• “Remove catheter within 30 minutes if edema is observed around insertion site.” – Remove infiltrated peripheral IV promptly

text: Question: The outpatient clinic nurse is planning to teach a client with a urinary tract infection who has a new prescription for ciprofloxacin-XR tablets, 500 mg, p.o., daily x 7 days.  Which of the following statements should the nurse make?

B. “Swallow the medication with a full glass of milk.”
C. "Complete the entire prescription even if you are feeling better.”
D. “Take an over-the-counter antacid 1 hour prior to taking the ciprofloxacin dose.”
Correct answer: C. "Complete the entire prescription even if you are feeling better.”
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• "Complete the entire prescription even if you are feeling better.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)

Not correct:
• ““Crush the tablet and mix with applesauce if the tablet is too large to swallow.”” – Crushing disrupts extended release
• ““Swallow the medication with a full glass of milk.”” – Milk alone can reduce absorption
• ““Take an over-the-counter antacid 1 hour prior to taking the ciprofloxacin dose.”” – Antacids bind drug; separate as instructed

text: Question: The nurse is providing care for a client who has a diagnosis of hypercalcemia.  Which of the following would be an expected finding? (Select all that apply.)
A. Trousseau's sign
B. weakness, lethargy
C. increased deep tendon reflexes
D. muscle spasm
E. kidney stones
F. dcreased reflexes
G. bone pain
Correct answers: B. weakness, lethargy; E. kidney stones; F. dcreased reflexes; G. bone pain
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• weakness, lethargy
• kidney stones
• dcreased reflexes
• bone pain
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “weakness, lethargy” – High calcium depresses neuromuscular activity
• “kidney stones” – Hypercalciuria can promote stones
• “dcreased reflexes” – Neuromuscular excitability decreases
• “bone pain” – May reflect underlying bone resorption
Not correct:
• “Trousseau's sign” – Suggests hypocalcemia
• “increased deep tendon reflexes” – Suggests hypocalcemia
• “muscle spasm” – Tetany more typical of low calcium
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 2 - Physiological Adaptation, slide 12: “Muscle weakness”
• Unit 2 - Physiological Adaptation, slide 12: “Deep bone pain”
• Unit 2 - Physiological Adaptation, slide 12: “Calcium stones”
• Unit 2 - Reduction of Risk Potential, slide 29: “Muscle twitching. Yes, a sign of hypocalcemia.”
Trousseau sign, muscle spasm and hyperactive reflexes are hypocalcemia signs on your Unit 2 slide, which rules those options out; decreased reflexes are not named on your slides.

text: Question: The nurse has received change-of-shift report about the following clients on the progressive care unit. Which client should the nurse see first?
A. A post aortic valvular repair client receiving warfarin and INR of 3.4
B. A client whose implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) fired two times today who has a dose of amiodarone due
C. A client with new onset atrial fibrillation, rate 88, who has a first dose of warfarin due
D. A client with pericarditis oral temperature is 101.2 F.
Correct answer: B. A client whose implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) fired two times today who has a dose of amiodarone due
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• A client whose implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) fired two times today who has a dose of amiodarone due
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “A client whose implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) fired two times today who h…” – Recurrent ICD shocks suggest important ventricular arrhythmia
Not correct:
• “A post aortic valvular repair client receiving warfarin and INR of 3.4” – INR may be appropriate depending on valve and target
• “A client with new onset atrial fibrillation, rate 88, who has a first dose of warfarin due” – Controlled rate makes this less urgent
• “A client with pericarditis oral temperature is 101.2 F.” – Fever needs evaluation but repeated shocks take priority

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a patient who develops marked edema and a low urine output as a result of heart failure. Which medication will the nurse expect the provider to order for this patient?
A. Hydrochlorothiazide
B. Digoxin
C. Spironolactone
D. Furosemide
Correct answer: D. Furosemide
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Furosemide
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Furosemide” – Loop diuretic promotes brisk fluid removal
Not correct:
• “Hydrochlorothiazide” – Less potent for marked congestion
• “Digoxin” – Improves contractility/rate but is not a diuretic
• “Spironolactone” – Weak diuretic relative to loop agents
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:

text: Question: A patient has been taking spironolactone to treat heart failure. The nurse will monitor for
